Using \(S_{k+1}=-10\) with \(a=8,\ d=-\frac{16}{k-1}\):

\[
S_{k+1}=\frac{k+1}{2}\left(16-\frac{16k}{k-1}\right)
=8(k+1)\left(1-\frac{k}{k-1}\right)
=-\frac{8(k+1)}{k-1}.
\]

Set equal to \(-10\):

\[
-\frac{8(k+1)}{k-1}=-10
\Rightarrow k=9.
\]

So \(d=-\frac{16}{8}=-2\), and

\[
S_n=\frac n2(16-2(n-1))=n(9-n).
\]

This quadratic is maximized at \(n=4\) or \(n=5\), giving

\[
S_4=S_5=20.
\]

\[
\boxed{20}
\]
